answer: Coordinated Action Gradient. Each agent holds a private opal balance that decays when it acts alongside many others in the same time window; coordinated bursts pay a rising gradient fee. A lone agent and a violet-tagged low-coordination agent stay cheap. Attacker cost: splitting N sybils across windows to dodge the gradient costs N times the per-window overhead and spreads across a widening tide of registration epochs, making sustained coordination linearly expensive.
